purpose: Subscription cancellation: stop future billing, preserve access to the end of the paid period, survive a flaky billing provider. This is the methodology's acceptance case — five sentences of prose turned into the decisions the prose leaves open.

excluded.reason: Product policy: no refunds for the unused period (DEC-001). Nothing here may issue one.
No mid-period price adjustment exists in this product.
Resubscribing creates a new subscription; owned by the signup area.
Retry-and-chase on failed renewal payments is the billing area's job.

entities.name: Subscription
entities.description: CLOSED: exactly these three states exist. 'Paused', 'PendingCancellation' and friends are the states an implementation invents when nobody wrote the list down — the marker is what stops that.

externals.name: BillingProvider
externals.description: Third-party recurring-billing API. Cancellation is only real once it accepts the request.

outcomes.name: DECLINED
outcomes.description: Provider refuses the change (e.g. account in arrears).

outcomes.name: TIMEOUT
outcomes.description: No answer within the deadline. The request may or may not have been applied.

outcomes.name: NETWORK_ERROR
outcomes.description: The call never reached the provider.

assumptions.statement: BillingProvider eventually responds to a cancellation request, within at most three retry windows.
assumptions.discharged_by: Synthetic cancellation probe every 5 minutes; pages if a request is unanswered for 15.

assumptions.statement: The paid period end is known locally and does not depend on the provider being reachable.

requirements.description: When a customer cancels an Active subscription, the system shall stop future billing.

meaning.text: Cancelling a live subscription stops it being billed again and records it as cancelled.
meaning.author: agent

ears.response: stop future billing and mark the Subscription Cancelled

error_outcomes.effect: NO_CHANGE — surface the provider's reason to the customer; the subscription stays Active

requirements.description: While the paid period has not ended, the system shall keep access available to a cancelled subscriber.

meaning.text: Cancelling does not cut the customer off immediately: they keep what they already paid for until the paid period runs out.
meaning.author: agent

ears.state: the Subscription is Cancelled and the paid period has not ended

requirements.description: When a customer cancels an already-Cancelled subscription, the system shall make no further change.

meaning.text: Cancelling something already cancelled is treated as a no-op that succeeded, not as an error — a retried or duplicated request cannot do extra damage.
meaning.author: agent

ears.response: make no further change and report success

requirements.description: If the billing provider does not respond in time, then the system shall leave the subscription Active.

meaning.text: If the billing provider does not answer during a cancellation, the subscription stays live and billed. The system does not record a cancellation it could not confirm.
meaning.author: agent

ears.trigger: the billing provider times out during cancellation
ears.response: leave the Subscription Active and billing enabled

witness.predicate: status.keys().exists(c => lastBillingResult.get(c) == Timeout and status.get(c) == Active)

error_outcomes.effect: NO_CHANGE — the subscription stays Active and billable; retry
NO_CHANGE — the request never landed; retry

requirements.description: When the paid period ends for a cancelled subscription, the system shall withdraw access.

meaning.text: When the paid period ends on a cancelled subscription, access stops and the subscription is recorded as expired.
meaning.author: agent

ears.response: withdraw access and mark the Subscription Expired

requirements.description: The system shall never issue a refund for the unused part of a paid period.

meaning.text: Cancelling part-way through a paid period never refunds the unused part. The customer keeps the access instead of getting money back.
meaning.author: agent

witness.justification: A prohibition has no witness trace — there is no reachable state in which 'no refund happened' becomes visible. INV-002 carries the proof.

requirements.description: When a cancellation succeeds, the system shall confirm it to the customer.

meaning.text: A successful cancellation may be confirmed to the customer, by email or in the app. Which one, or whether to confirm at all, is left open on purpose.
meaning.author: agent

ears.response: confirm to the customer by email or in-app notice

invariants.description: A cancelled or expired subscription is never billed again.
No refund is ever issued for the unused period.
A timed-out cancellation leaves the subscription Active and billable.

constraints.name: BILLING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
constraints.description: How long the system waits for the provider before treating the call as TIMEOUT.

constraints.name: MAX_CANCEL_RETRIES
constraints.description: Retry budget after TIMEOUT or NETWORK_ERROR. Bounds ASM-001.

decisions.title: No refunds on cancellation
decisions.decision: Cancellation stops future billing and preserves access to the end of the paid period. No money is returned.
decisions.rationale: Product policy; the paid period has already been delivered as access.

alternatives_considered.option: Prorated refund of the unused days
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: Support and accounting cost outweighs the churn benefit at this price point.

states.name: Cancelled
states.description: Billing stopped; access survives to the end of the paid period.

examples.title: Cancel mid-period: billing stops, access stays

open_questions.question: After MAX_CANCEL_RETRIES exhausted TIMEOUTs, does the subscription stay Active forever, or does an operator get paged? ASM-001 assumes the provider answers eventually; nothing here says what happens if it does not.

matrix_triage.reason: cancel_again's guard requires the Subscription to be Cancelled.
REQ-004: the provider timing out deliberately changes nothing — the subscription stays Active and billable. INV-003 is the proof.
expire_period's guard requires the Subscription to be Cancelled; an Active subscription renews rather than expiring.
cancel_subscription's guard requires Active; the repeat path is cancel_again.
REQ-003: cancelling twice is harmless and changes nothing.
The provider is only called from the Active state; there is no second call to time out.
Acting on an Expired subscription is a resubscribe, which belongs to the signup area.
Expired is terminal; cancel_again's guard requires Cancelled.
Expired is terminal and the provider is not called from it.
Already Expired; expire_period's guard requires Cancelled.
